accepted.question_text: For each integer n >= 0 and each r in [0,1), determine the exact operator norms of I - K_n and I - P_r on the Lebesgue spaces L^p(T) for 1 < p < infinity, and on the Hardy spaces H^p(T) for 1 <= p <= infinity, where K_n is convolution with the n-th Fejer kernel on the unit circle T and P_r is convolution with the Poisson kernel.
accepted.context_brief: Exact norms of Fejer and Poisson approximation operators

evidence.quote: For theta in [-pi, pi] and n = 0, 1, 2, . . . , let K_n(e^{i theta}) := sum_{k=-n}^n (1 - |k|/(n + 1)) e^{ik theta} = 1/(n + 1) (sin ((n+1)theta/2) / sin (theta/2))^2, be the n-th Fejer kernel, and let K_n f := K_n * f, f in X.
Consider also the operators I - P_r, where P_r f := P_r * f, 0 <= r < 1, and P_r is the Poisson kernel.

Open problem 5.2. Let n in Z_+ and r in [0, 1). Find the exact values of ||I - K_n||_{B(L^p)} and ||I - P_r||_{B(L^p)} for 1 < p < infinity, and of ||I - K_n||_{B(H^p)} and ||I - P_r||_{B(H^p)} for 1 <= p <= infinity.

accepted.question_text: For each 1 <= p < infinity, determine the exact operator norm of the backward shift B on the Hardy space H^p(T), where B acts by Bf(e^{i theta}) = e^{-i theta}(f(e^{i theta}) - f_hat(0)).
accepted.context_brief: Backward shift norm on Hardy spaces

evidence.quote: We think that the question about the exact value of ||I - K_0||_{B(H^p)} is particularly interesting, and although it is a special case of Problem 5.2, we state it again below in terms of the backward shift operator (Bf)(e^{i theta}) := e^{-i theta}(f(e^{i theta}) - f_hat(0)) = e^{-i theta}((I - K_0)f)(e^{i theta}), f in H^p.
Open problem 5.4. Let 1 <= p < infinity. Find the exact value of the norm ||B||_{B(H^p)} of the backward shift operator.

accepted.question_text: Determine the exact bounded compact approximation constant M(H^p) for every 1 <= p < infinity, and determine the exact dual compact approximation constant M*(H^p) for every 1 < p < infinity, where M(H^p) is the greatest lower bound of the constants M for which every finite subset of H^p can be approximated pointwise by a compact operator T with ||I - T|| <= M, and M*(H^p) is the analogous greatest lower bound defined through approximation of finite subsets of the dual space by adjoints of compact operators.
accepted.context_brief: Exact BCAP and DCAP constants for H^p

evidence.quote: A Banach space E is said to have the bounded compact approximation property (BCAP) if there exists a constant M in (0, infinity) such that given any epsilon > 0 and any finite set F subset E, there exists an operator T in K(E) such that ||I - T||_{B(E)} <= M, ||y - Ty||_E < epsilon for all y in F.
The greatest lower bound of the constants M for which (1.3) holds will be denoted by M(E).

A Banach space E with the dual space E* is said to have the dual compact approximation property (DCAP) if there is a constant M* in (0, infinity) such that given any epsilon > 0 and any finite set G subset E*, there exists an operator T in K(E) such that ||I - T||_{B(E)} <= M*, ||z - T*z||_{E*} < epsilon for all z in G.
The greatest lower bound of the constants M*, for which (1.4) holds, will be denoted by M*(E).
Open problem 5.5. (a) Find the exact value of M(H^p), 1 <= p < infinity. (b) Find the exact value of M*(H^p), 1 < p < infinity.

accepted.question_text: For each 1 <= p < infinity, decide whether the bounded compact approximation constant M(H^p) is equal to the operator norm of the map f -> f - f_hat(0) on H^p(T), equivalently whether M(H^p) = ||I - K_0||_{B(H^p)}, where K_0 is the Fejer operator at n = 0.
accepted.context_brief: Relation between BCAP constant and zeroth-mode projection

evidence.quote: For n = 0, one has (I - K_0)f = f - f_hat(0) = (I - P_0)f and ||I - K_0||_{B(L^p)} = C_p, but the value of ||I - K_0||_{B(H^p)} does not seem to be known for p in [1, infinity) \ {2}.
Given that M(L^p) = ||I - K_0||_{B(L^p)} (see [25, Theorem 3.2]), it would be interesting to know whether M(H^p) = ||I - K_0||_{B(H^p)}.

accepted.question_text: Let L_{p,q} be the Lorentz space on the unit circle T for 1 <= q <= p < infinity, and let H[L_{p,q}] be the associated Hardy-Lorentz space. Determine a nontrivial lower bound for the bounded compact approximation constant M(H[L_{p,q}]) and improve the known upper bound M(H[L_{p,q}]) <= 2. Also, for 1 < q <= p < infinity, determine a nontrivial lower bound for the dual compact approximation constant M*(H[L_{p,q}]) and improve the known upper bound M*(H[L_{p,q}]) <= 2.
accepted.context_brief: Bounds for BCAP and DCAP on Hardy-Lorentz spaces

evidence.quote: For 1 <= q <= p < infinity, the Lorentz space L_{p,q} consists of all measurable functions f : T -> C for which ||f||_{p,q} := (integral_0^1 [t^{1/p} f*(t)]^q dt/t)^{1/q} < infinity.

It follows from Theorem 3.3 that if 1 <= q <= p < infinity, then the Hardy-Lorentz space H[L_{p,q}] has the BCAP with M(H[L_{p,q}]) <= 2, because L_{p,q} is separable in this case. Moreover, if 1 < q <= p < infinity, then the Hardy-Lorentz space H[L_{p,q}] has the DCAP with M*(H[L_{p,q}]) <= 2, since the Lorentz space L_{p,q} is reflexive in this case.

Open problem 5.8. (a) Let 1 <= q <= p < infinity. Find a nontrivial lower bound for M(H[L_{p,q}]). Improve the upper bound for M(H[L_{p,q}]) given by (5.9). (b) Let 1 < q <= p < infinity. Find a nontrivial lower bound for M*(H[L_{p,q}]). Improve the upper bound for M*(H[L_{p,q}]) given by (5.10).

needs_review.question_text_raw: Given that the value of M(H^p) is not known, it would perhaps be too ambitious to ask about the exact values of M(H[L_phi]) and M*(H[L_phi]). Nevertheless, we think it would be interesting to get more information on these quantities.
